title: Man. Post. Cap. IX: PLAC — 'we did not sin actu in original sin except as in Adam' — did we sin actu when he did?
pass_a_gloss: Placeus presses Garrigues's line that in original sin we did not sin actu except as in Adam: does that mean we actually sinned in Adam at the moment he sinned?
pass_b_english: For the rest I do not well enough understand those words of yours: "In original sin we did not sin by act, except insofar as we sinned in Adam." What then? Do you mean that we sinned by act in Adam at the time when he sinned?
source_text: Caeterum non satis intelligo tua ista verba, In peccato originali non peccavimus actu, nisi quatenus in Adamo peccavimus. Quid enim? Visne nos actu peccavisse in Adamo tum cum peccavit?

choices.choice: Did we sin actu in Adam when he sinned?

notes: Cap. IX aptitudo densify section 632 from locked 1661 Latin (pp. 352–353 tip).
